subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Galaxy Clusters
description: A quick, practical guide to Galaxy Clusters.

hook.text: Galaxy clusters contain hundreds to thousands of galaxies bound together by gravity. They're the largest bound structures.

buildup.text: The Virgo Cluster is the nearest large cluster—about 1,300 galaxies located 54 million light-years away.

discovery.text: Fritz Zwicky studied the Coma Cluster in 1933 and found it needed far more mass than visible. He proposed dark matter.

twist.text: Most of a cluster's normal matter is not in galaxies—it's in hot gas between them, glowing in X-rays at millions of degrees.

climax.text: Clusters act as cosmic laboratories for studying dark matter, hot gas physics, and galaxy evolution all at once.

punchline.text: Thousands of galaxies in one structure. Mostly held together by invisible mass.

quiz.question: Where is most of the normal matter in a galaxy cluster?
options: In hot gas between the galaxies, glowing in X-rays
Inside the galaxies themselves as stars
In the dark matter halo surrounding the cluster

details.summary: Galaxy clusters are the largest gravitationally bound structures in the universe, containing hundreds to thousands of galaxies, hot X-ray-emitting gas, and vast amounts of dark matter — all spanning 10-30 million light-years.
details.whyItMatters: Galaxy clusters are cosmic laboratories for studying dark matter, galaxy evolution, and the large-scale structure of the universe. Their abundance and growth rate constrain fundamental cosmological parameters.
takeaways: Largest gravitationally bound structures in the universe
Contain hundreds to thousands of galaxies plus hot gas
Dark matter dominates their total mass

faq.question: What is the intracluster medium?
faq.answer: The hot gas filling the space between cluster galaxies, heated to tens of millions of degrees by gravitational compression. It emits X-rays and contains more baryonic mass than all the cluster's galaxies combined — about 5-10 times more. It's detected by X-ray telescopes like Chandra and XMM-Newton.

faq.question: What is the largest known galaxy cluster?
faq.answer: El Gordo (ACT-CL J0102-4915) is one of the most massive known distant clusters. The Shapley Supercluster concentration contains several massive clusters. Locally, the Coma Cluster and Virgo Cluster are among the best studied.
